disease_label_per_paper: Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome linked to a novel C73Y TNFRSF1A mutation
presentation_summary: Nine-year-old girl was admitted with two months of fever and generalized malaise, associated at onset with intermittent abdominal pain, migratory myalgia, and throat pain.

She was petite with somatometric features below the third centile and had a history of prolonged pyrexia admissions at 12 and 26 months, arthritis at 7 and 8 years, and additional short fever episodes 1-2 times per year.
Family history was strongly suggestive: her father and several paternal relatives had fever, arthritis, serositis, abdominal pain, or similar recurrent inflammatory symptoms.
Initial evaluation found no clear infectious source and showed mesenteric lymphadenitis, myositis/fasciitis of the left major gluteal muscle, and corneal sediments due to uveitis.
Laboratory data showed WBC 23,200/uL with 81% neutrophils, ESR 117 mm/hr, CRP 261 mg/L, ferritin 421 ng/mL, fibrinogen 6.21 g/L, SAA 590 mg/L, and hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL.
TNFRSF1A genetic testing, family cascade testing, steroid/canakinumab response, and final diagnostic interpretation are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.
